ai.description: This small frog (20–25 mm) is pale yellow to lime green with a translucent belly. It features a distinct white spot on the snout and lacks vomerine teeth. Family: Rhacophoridae. IUCN: LC.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes luteolus* is best distinguished by its uniform, bright lemon-yellow to greenish-yellow dorsal coloration, which lacks the distinct dark markings found in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Coorg Yellow Bush Frog inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Coorg Yellow Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the foliage of the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes luteolus* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They lay small clutches of terrestrial eggs in tree holes during the monsoon (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: The Coorg Yellow Bush Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Karnataka and Kerala at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Coorg Yellow Bush Frog produces a high-pitched, insect-like "tink-tink" call, typically heard from vegetation in evergreen forests and coffee plantations.
